messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The proposed model outperforms other models when trained on the LDC2017T10 dataset, as evidenced by its state-of-the-art single model performance on both datasets." -- cites: E2 (Section 4): quote "Our results show that adding syntax into the model dramatically boosts performance, resulting in state-of-the-art single model performance on both datasets without using external training data."
2. "The performance of the proposed model is significantly enhanced by incorporating syntax, as shown by the dramatic boost in BLEU scores when using an oracle parse." -- cites: E2 (Section 4): quote "The outstanding result here – BLEU scores in the 50s – demonstrates that being able to predict the gold reference parse tree is a bottleneck in the performance of our model."
3. "The proposed model's performance on the LDC2017T10 dataset is comparable to other models trained on earlier datasets, but it does not match the performance of models trained on more recent datasets or those using additional unlabelled data." -- cites: E3 (Section Table 3): quote "Our model 26.1 26.8"; E3 (Section Table 3): quote "Our model 23.6 23.5"; E3 (Section Table 3): quote "Song et al. (2018) 22.8 23.3"

Cited evidence:
[E2] (text, Section 4, page 4): AMR-to-text model with the same architecture as above to control for the extra regularisation in our model compared to previous work. Our results show that adding syntax into the model dramatically boosts performance, resulting in state-ofthe-art single model performance on both datasets without using external training data. As an oracle experiment, we also generate from the realisation model conditioned on the ground truth parse. The outstanding result here – BLEU scores in the 50s – demonstrates that being able to predict the gold reference parse tree is a bottleneck in the performance of our model. However, given the inherent difﬁculty of predicting a single syntax realisation (cf. Section 4 ), we suspect that there is an intrinsic limit to how well generating from an AMR graph can replicate the reference realisation. We further note that we do not use models tailored to graph-structured data or characterlevel features as in Song et al. ( 2018 ); Beck et al. ( 2018 ), or additional unlabelled data to perform semi-supervised learning ( Konstas et al. , 2017 ). We believe that we can improve our results even further if we use these techniques.

verdicts.reason: The claim states that the proposed model outperforms other models on the LDC2017T10 dataset, but the evidence only mentions state-of-the-art performance on both datasets without using external training data. The claim also mentions both datasets, while the evidence only refers to one dataset.

The claim attributes the performance enhancement to incorporating syntax, but the evidence states that the dramatic boost in BLEU scores is due to being able to predict the gold reference parse tree, not the incorporation of syntax.

The claim suggests that the proposed model's performance is comparable to other models trained on earlier datasets and does not match more recent datasets or those using additional unlabelled data. The evidence only compares the model's performance on the LDC2017T10 dataset to other models trained on the same dataset and does not provide a comparison to more recent datasets or those using additional unlabelled data.
